headline: US Treasury's Bessent: Stronger yen is better for US exporters

evidence.dominant_driver: Renewed explicit US Treasury support for a stronger yen and confirmation of US-Japan intervention coordination.

market_expectations.distribution_notes: BOJ September hike expectations are already elevated; Reuters reporting showed an 80% probability context.

absorption.reason: The yen-support/intervention stance is not new and Tokyo cash trading had already closed; USD/JPY had traded around 154.9 during Tokyo hours.

observations.USDJPY: Around 154.9 in late Tokyo trade, weaker yen on the day despite policy support rhetoric.
observations.oil: WTI about 103, Brent about 106.08; high energy costs remain a Japan headwind.

evidence.decision_notes: Residual forecast only. Cash Nikkei is closed; fixed 15m/1h/4h horizons are not substituted with the next cash open. M2 learning profile has no ACTIONABLE model-2 segment applicable here, so confidence is unchanged.

immediate.rationale: Tokyo cash market is closed and the yen-support stance is partly known; no clean residual 15m directional edge.

next_session.rationale: If the stronger-yen policy signal carries into Tokyo, exporter-heavy Nikkei constituents face a valuation/earnings translation headwind.

15m.rationale: Cash market closed; incremental rhetoric is partly priced and cannot produce a clean cash-index reaction now.

1h.rationale: No fresh cash-session confirmation; USD/JPY context conflicts with the stronger-yen message.

4h.rationale: Policy support for yen is bearish for exporters, but the signal is not new and pre-BOJ positioning can dominate.

next_session.rationale: A renewed yen-strength impulse would pressure exporter-heavy Nikkei at the next Tokyo session.

predictions.mechanism: Stronger yen reduces translated overseas earnings and competitiveness for Japanese exporters; intervention coordination raises the probability of yen-support action.
predictions.invalidation: USD/JPY resumes a sustained rise above the recent 155 area or BOJ expectations turn materially less hawkish before Tokyo opens.
predictions.counter_case: The comment may be dismissed as repetition; if USD/JPY stays firm and global tech stabilizes, Nikkei can rise despite yen-support rhetoric.

technical_state.session_location: Tokyo cash closed after a nearly flat session
